---
title: "Regression"
---

These materials introduce regression as a way to translate an observed
engineering relationship into a quantitative prediction. We continue to use
the course gas-turbine emissions dataset, beginning with a single, interpretable
question before adding the complications of multiple predictors and model
validation.

We highly recommend working with Google Colab. It lets you run the notebooks
in the cloud without local setup.

## 1. Simple linear regression: weather and NOx

**Estimated time:** 45–60 minutes

Use ambient temperature to predict NOx concentration, fit a least-squares
line, and distinguish a statistically significant association from a causal
claim or a complete engineering model.

[View the notebook](01-simple-linear-regression.ipynb)

## 2. Uncertainty in a regression slope

The interactive explorer and notebook work together: first make the variability
of a fitted slope visible, then connect it to standard errors, confidence
intervals, and hypothesis tests.

### Interactive explorer

**Estimated time:** 10–15 minutes

Draw repeated samples of real turbine operating hours, watch fitted lines
accumulate, and compare the spread of their slopes.

[Open the interactive explorer](sampling-variability.qmd)

### Notebook

**Estimated time:** 50–65 minutes

Use repeated samples to see why the temperature–NOx slope is an estimate, then
quantify its uncertainty with a standard error, confidence interval, and
hypothesis test.

[View the notebook](02-testing-a-regression-slope.ipynb)
